dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about your family.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: For the majority to live a life of peace, a minority of people must make great sacrifices. My family belong to this minority.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: But this we have known since the day that we received orders from Lady Vennessa herself.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: ...Have you heard of Barbatos Ratatouille? It is said to have been one of the dishes served at the feast held in celebration after Vennessa defeated the old aristocracy.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: My forebears had the honor of dining with Vennessa that day. After the feast, an accomplished chef was invited to taste the dish and infer the recipe.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: The taste is like the gentle caress of the breeze on your cheeks, and you can almost feel the peace and freedom given by Barbatos welling up inside your heart... That dish has kept our family going over the centuries as we watch out for storms, day in, day out.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: ...Thank you for listening to me. In fact, here, please have the recipe. It's my pleasure to share the joy of this wonderful dish with you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The past?

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: As you can see, looking out from the watchtower, the seas around Mondstadt are calm and peaceful.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: Since those days went by, Lord Barbatos has been protecting Mondstadt. There have been no storms ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: Even our family has not seen a true storm for many generations.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So why do you still keep watch here?

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: Maybe it's because every beacon longs for its time to shine.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: Even if I knew for certain that there would never be a single storm again, once in a while my mind would be drawn to the stories they used to tell in my father's generation...

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: The way our ancestors would defiantly blow the horn in the middle of a raging storm, sending a warning signal to all in Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: And when I came back out of my reverie... I would find that I had walked all the way here, without realizing.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: Could it be that you share my interest in storms?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: It's so rare to find a traveler passing through a remote out-of-the-way place like this.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: I'm Vind, devoted follower of Lord Barbatos.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: My family was given an order by Lady Vennessa. We are to keep watch here, looking out over the sea for any sign of an oncoming storm.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: For generations, everyone in my family has felt honored to have this duty.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: We see it as our life's purpose to be signal beacons for Mondstadt, ready to spread the message to every corner of Mondstadt at the first sign of a storm.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: But... That's all in the past, now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: Farewell, unknown traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Vind
dialogues.text: May Barbatos' gentle wind be with you.
